subject: Can this be done by faceting?

messages.author: 62f725013dca6cda
messages.subject: Can this be done by faceting?
parts:
Folks,
  Sorry to bother you all again!

I have chosen 4 sample scenarios from a large time-series simulation. Each scenario is a pair of correlated paths (these are economic/financial variables): one is a path of GDP and the other is a path of defaults on credit card balances.

I would like to plot these 4 scenarios (again: each scenario contains two time-series) in a 2x2 configuration where each sub-chart has the same x/y (min, max).

My guess is that I need a data.frame that has 5 columns: Date, Facet1 (value 1 or 2), Facet2 (value 1 or 2), GDP, Default

If there is an easier way to do this please let me know,
Thanks (once again),
KW

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: Can this be done by faceting?
parts:
That sounds like it will work fine, though if Facet1 and Facet2 are
arbitrary and just being used to produce the 2x2 grid, you'll want to
remove the facet labels using +opts(...).

Ben
